subject.title: feat(acp): pipe lifeline — reap the bridge tree on abrupt owner death

question: Should acpx adopt this POSIX native pipe-lifeline and lazy-compiled helper as the supported bridge lifecycle model for abrupt owner death?
rationale: The patch has no concrete code finding left, but only maintainers can accept the long-term operating contract around native helper compilation, process-group signals, POSIX-only behavior, and the env override.

options.title: Accept the lifeline contract
options.body: Treat the POSIX helper and lazy compile/cache path as the supported best-effort lifecycle model and merge after maintainer review.

options.title: Split the lifecycle change
options.body: Land cooperative process-group close cleanup separately and decide abrupt owner-death reaping in a narrower follow-up.

options.title: Pause for native policy
options.body: Hold or close the PR until maintainers define whether runtime native compilation and helper override env vars belong in acpx core.

recommendation.title: Accept the lifeline contract
recommendation.body: Treat the POSIX helper and lazy compile/cache path as the supported best-effort lifecycle model and merge after maintainer review.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent queue-owner shutdown history makes steipete the strongest available owner for accepting or rejecting the process-lifecycle contract.
